title: Simultaneous analyses of clutch coupling and actin polymerization in dendritic spines of rodent hippocampal neurons during chemical LTP
protocol: Dilute 1 μL of TMR ligand in 200 μL of PBS as a working stock.
Collect 180 μL of conditioned medium from cultured neurons.
Mix collected conditioned medium with 20 μL of TMR ligand working stock.
Replace conditioned medium of cultured neurons with the TMR ligand-medium mixture.
Incubate at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 1 h.
Wash TMR ligand 3 times with pre-warmed PBS.
Incubate neurons with 500 μL of pre-warmed ACSF containing MgCl2, 0.5 μM tetrodotoxin, 1 μM strychnine, and 20 μM bicuculline at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 1 h.
Perform time-lapse imaging of dendritic spines before and after chemical long-term potentiation (cLTP).
Set the stage-top incubator of the microscope at 37°C.
Transfer TMR ligand-treated neurons into the incubator.
Select neurons that are strongly expressing Lifeact and weakly expressing HaloTag-actin.
Adjust the optimum exposure times of Lifeact and HaloTag-actin filter channels.
Close the field of the microscope diaphragm to illuminate only a minimum area including a dendritic spine.
Illuminate the target spine without using neutral density filters to increase the signal-to-noise ratio.
Acquire single plane time-lapse images of a spine for both HaloTag-actin and Lifeact every 2 seconds for 100 seconds.
Replace ACSF solution containing MgCl2 with freshly prepared glycine stimulation solution and incubate for 4 minutes to induce cLTP.
Avoid touching the dish when replacing solutions to prevent a shift in spine location.
Pre-warm glycine stimulation solution and ACSF without MgCl2 before replacement to minimize focus drift due to thermal changes.
Replace the glycine stimulation solution with ACSF without MgCl2 immediately after inducing cLTP.
Acquire time-lapse images every 2 seconds for 100 seconds following the replacement of solutions.
